title: Topology-aware Embedding Memory for Continual Learning on Expanding Networks

problem.claim: Continual learning on expanding networks can cause memory explosion because representative nodes and their associated topological neighborhood structures must be buffered.

gap.claim: Memory replay techniques successful for incrementally accumulated Euclidean data do not directly address memory explosion in continually expanding networks.

contributions.claim: A general framework combining Parameter Decoupled Graph Neural Networks with Topology-aware Embedding Memory is presented to address memory explosion.
Topology-aware Embeddings compress ego-subnetworks into compact vectors, decoupling trainable parameters from the computation ego-subnetwork to reduce memory consumption.
A coverage maximization sampling strategy is developed to improve continual learning performance under a tight memory budget.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the coverage maximization sampling strategy as novel and identify a unique pseudo-training effect in continual learning on expanding networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework is reported to reduce memory space complexity from O(ndL) to O(n), where d is average node degree and L is the GNN receptive-field radius.
The authors report that PDGNNs with TEM significantly outperform state-of-the-art techniques, especially in the class-incremental setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Memory replay has been successful for continual learning with incrementally accumulated Euclidean data.
Applying those techniques to expanding networks creates a potential memory explosion problem.
The authors analyze the challenge and present PDGNNs with TEM as a general framework.
The framework reduces memory complexity, preserves topological information for replay, and uses topology-aware embeddings to compress ego-subnetworks.
A pseudo-training effect motivates coverage maximization sampling, and empirical studies report improvements over state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: Compressing ego-subnetworks into topology-aware embedding vectors reduces the reported memory complexity while retaining topological information for replay.

interpretation.claim: When structured neighborhood data drives memory growth, a compact representation may preserve useful structure while avoiding direct storage of the full neighborhoods.

application.claim: For continual learning over growing relational data, consider storing topology-aware representations instead of complete representative neighborhoods.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the compression preserves all task-relevant information or generalizes beyond the reported settings.

source_observation.claim: A pseudo-training effect motivates coverage maximization sampling under a tight memory budget.

interpretation.claim: Sampling coverage may matter in continual learning when limited memory must represent changing network structure.

application.claim: Under constrained replay memory, evaluate sampling strategies that maximize coverage of relevant network structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the pseudo-training effect, the coverage objective, or the conditions under which the sampling strategy is effective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative performance values.
The abstract does not define the pseudo-training effect or the coverage maximization objective in detail.
The abstract does not report implementation details, training settings, or computational trade-offs.
